## Verdict

wrong

## Bearer

PreparationUiState — app-wear/src/main/java/com/mgilli/app_wear/preparation/PreparationUiState.kt

## Trigger

PreparationViewModel.applyState() mapping a `PreparationState` outcome
into a `PreparationUiState`, and `PreparationScreen.kt`'s `when` block
rendering that state — observed

## Today

`PreparationUiState` declares `OpenFailed` as a case distinct from
`Ready`, but both carry the same `heartRateText: String?` and
`PreparationScreen.kt:34-48` renders both through the very same
`ReadyContent` composable, with the same labels and no failure text.
`Ready(heartRateText = null)` and `OpenFailed(heartRateText = null)`
therefore produce identical pixels: a session that failed to open
looks exactly like one that is open and simply has not yet heard from
the sensor. `PreparationViewModel.mutableUiState` also starts at
`null` (`:48`), and `PreparationScreen.kt:32` renders `null -> Unit`
— the same blank screen "nothing collected yet" and "the source
failed on its first emission" both produce.

Upstream of this, `ExerciseSessionOpenResult`
(app-wear/src/main/java/com/mgilli/app_wear/sensor/session/ExerciseSessionOpenResult.kt)
carries `Opened`, `Adopted`, `DeviceSlotTaken` and `Failed` only. In
`ExerciseSessionSystemImpl.startExerciseSession()`
(app-wear/src/main/java/com/mgilli/app_wear/sensor/session/ExerciseSessionSystemImpl.kt:52-64),
every exception the session start throws — including a permission
refusal — is caught by one generic `catch (other: Exception)` and
mapped to `ExerciseSessionStartOutcome.Failed`, then to
`ExerciseSessionOpenResult.Failed` in
`ExerciseSessionManager.open()`. `RaceLaunchController.mapOpenResult()`
maps that single `Failed` outcome to the single
`PreparationState.OpenFailed`, so a permission refusal and any other
transient sensor failure reach the screen as the same state.

The same hole exists on the main race page: `MainRacePageUiState`
(app-wear/src/main/java/com/mgilli/app_wear/race/MainRacePageUiState.kt)
has no case meaning "the exercise session failed" — only
`SensorValueDisplay.Fresh`, `Stale` and `Fallback`.
`MainRacePageViewModel.computeState()` (`:357-363`) returns
`SensorValueDisplay.Fallback` whenever no heart-rate reading is fresh
or stale-and-visible, whether that is because none has arrived yet or
because the session that would produce one never opened. No state
anywhere in `:app-wear` can carry "the exercise session failed to
open."

## Expected

`PreparationUiState` carries a case for a failed session open that
`PreparationScreen.kt` renders through a body distinct from
`ReadyContent` — not the same heart-rate label with nothing filled
in — and that case is reachable on `mutableUiState`'s first emission,
not only after a prior `Ready` has already been shown. Symmetrically,
`MainRacePageUiState` carries a case, distinct from
`SensorValueDisplay.Fallback`, meaning the exercise session is known
to have failed rather than simply not yet having produced a reading.

For either screen to reach that case, `ExerciseSessionOpenResult`
needs a case of its own for a permission refusal, distinct from
`Failed` — `ExerciseSessionSystemImpl.startExerciseSession()`'s
generic catch has to distinguish the permission exception from any
other before this can propagate through
`RaceLaunchController.mapOpenResult()` into `PreparationState` and
then into both screens' ui-state types. Until §10 names a text key for
either new case, R80 leaves the screen's wording a product decision;
the log of R79 is what a lot can rely on meanwhile.
